items.stem: Why prefer a native <button> element over a clickable <div> for an action?

options.text: It is keyboard-operable and announced correctly by assistive tech by default
options.rationale: Correct: native buttons bring focusability, keyboard activation and correct role for free.
Divs can be styled; the issue is semantics and behaviour.
Performance is not the reason; accessibility semantics are.

options.text: ARIA is impossible on a div
options.rationale: ARIA can be added to a div, but recreating full button behaviour is error-prone.

items.explanation: Correct: native buttons bring focusability, keyboard activation and correct role for free.

items.stem: When a modal dialog opens, correct focus management should:

options.text: Move focus into the dialog, trap it there, and restore it on close
options.rationale: Correct: focus should move in, stay within the dialog, and return to the trigger on close.

options.text: Leave focus on the page behind the modal
options.rationale: Leaving focus behind lets keyboard users interact with hidden content.

options.text: Remove focus from the page entirely
options.rationale: Focus must land somewhere usable, not be lost.

options.text: Hide the dialog from screen readers
options.rationale: The active dialog must be available to screen readers.

items.explanation: Correct: focus should move into the dialog, be trapped, and return to the trigger on close.

items.stem: Which TWO reflect correct use of ARIA? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use native HTML semantics first and ARIA only to fill gaps
options.rationale: Correct: the first rule of ARIA is to prefer native semantics.

options.text: Keep ARIA states like aria-expanded in sync with the UI
options.rationale: Correct: ARIA states must reflect the real current state.
That is redundant ARIA duplicating native semantics.

options.text: Use ARIA to hide required visible focus styles
options.rationale: ARIA is not for removing focus indicators; visible focus is required.

items.explanation: Correct: prefer native semantics and keep ARIA states synchronised with the UI.
